segs.text: Imagine owning a tiny slice of a building in Bengaluru. Not the whole thing. Just five hundred rupees' worth.
parts: Imagine owning a tiny slice of a building in Bengaluru.
Not the whole thing. Just five hundred rupees' worth.

segs.text: Today, that's almost impossible. Big assets come in big pieces, and buying them means paperwork, middlemen, and days of waiting.
parts: Big assets come in big pieces, and buying them means paperwork, middlemen, and days of waiting.

segs.text: Tokenization changes the packaging. Ownership of a real asset is recorded on a blockchain, as digital tokens.
parts: Ownership of a real asset is recorded on a blockchain, as digital tokens.

segs.text: Each token is a share of the real thing. A building, a government bond, gold, even art.
parts: Each token is a share of the real thing.
A building, a government bond, gold, even art.

segs.text: Because it lives on a shared ledger, ownership can be split into small pieces, traded at any hour, and settled in minutes instead of days.
parts: Because it lives on a shared ledger, ownership can be split into small pieces,
and settled in minutes instead of days.

segs.text: This is already happening. More than ten billion dollars of US Treasury bonds have been tokenized.
parts: More than ten billion dollars of US Treasury bonds have been tokenized.

segs.text: But a token is only as good as the promise behind it. Someone still has to hold the real asset, and the law has to recognise your claim.
parts: But a token is only as good as the promise behind it.
Someone still has to hold the real asset, and the law has to recognise your claim.

segs.text: Tokenization doesn't make things more valuable. It makes ownership easier to divide, move and verify.
parts: Tokenization doesn't make things more valuable.
It makes ownership easier to divide, move and verify.

segs.text: So, that slice of a building in Bengaluru? One day, it could be just a tap away.
parts: So, that slice of a building in Bengaluru?
One day, it could be just a tap away.
